newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Taiwan gives Gambia cash for health workers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan gives Gambia cash for health workers.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign minister, John Chang, gave Gambia $411,500 on Wednesday to pay salaries of foreign medical experts and to refurbish army barracks in the capital and inland, officials said.
Chang arrived in this tiny West African nation late on Monday and held talks with President Yahya Jammeh. He left on Wednesday for Guinea Bissau.
The medical experts come from Cuba, Egypt and Nigeria.
Chang's African tour has already taken him to South Africa, which is breaking diplomatic ties with Taipei in favour of China. China regards Taiwan as a renegade province.

Gambia opted for ties with Taiwan a year after Jammeh and fellow army officers toppled civilian independence leader Sir Dawda Jawara in 1994, alienating the tourist nation's traditional Western allies.
China suspended ties with Gambia after it recognised Taiwan.
Taiwan has financed projects ranging from a hospital to schools, roads and farming. Aid to date amounts to $40 million.
President Nelson Mandela announced in November that South Africa would scrap diplomatic recognition of Taiwan.
